biography.plain_text: Michael Lyons Lord is an American oil and gas executive who has led Lyons Petroleum Reserves in Texas. He also served as a manager of NCL Appalachia, an operator of gas fields in the eastern United States. Lyons Petroleum Reserves joined other sellers in an Appalachian asset sale to Ultra Resources.

long_biography.plain_text:
Gas executive Michael Lord sought producing fields with long operating lives and established customers. As a manager of NCL Appalachia, he helped oversee a venture that acquired roughly 1,200 wells in Pennsylvania and Ohio in 2005. The purchase also brought undeveloped drilling sites, allowing the partners to plan further production alongside existing output.

The venture paired an operating team with institutional capital: GE held the majority partnership interest, while NCL Appalachia managed the fields. Gathering lines connected the wells to buyers. Ohio production served regional industrial customers; Pennsylvania gas reached wider markets through connections to four major pipelines.

Full Michael Lyons Lord is the input display name. Public corporate and business sources generally use Michael Lord or Michael L. Lord. The match relies on exact vessel/company/geographic convergence, not the presence of Lyons in unrelated BBC or parliamentary text.

Black Swan is the 2013 34.1 m Westport ex-Lyons Pride, matching input 245 GT; the input 2012 start can represent construction. Latitudes is the later34.1 m228 GT Westport also named Lyons Pride; public sources differ between 2016 and 2017 delivery. The two vessels were not conflated. Neither is current in the immutable input.

CorporationWiki's person page was available as cached content and expressly lists NCL Appalachia membership, while its company-detail link now returns a domain-transfer notice. This weakens freshness and provenance; membership is treated as historical secondary evidence and is not converted to a known individual percentage.

The Energy and broad Self-made conclusions are transparent medium-confidence inferences from membership, venture formation and substantial gas operations. GE's 95% limited-partner stake and NCL's 5% general-partner stake are corporate interests, not Lord's personal percentages. The $400.384m contract price belongs to multiple sellers and is not his proceeds or net worth.

Current holdings are insufficiently mapped. The 2022 mineral roll confirms corporate royalty interests at a matching Woodlands business contact location, but its limited entries cannot establish personal ownership, aggregate value or principal-wealth materiality. The origin-sector fallback is therefore explicit.

Family background, source of launch capital, ownership of Lyons Petroleum at formation, education, exact date/place of birth and secondary nationality were not established. Neither independent nor advantaged self-made subtype is supported.

Priority LinkedIn, Instagram and personal-website searches used full name, shorter name, Texas geography and both company names. No attributable personal profile was found. Broader Facebook, X/Twitter, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia, Flickr, Vimeo, Trip Advisor and Zillow searches did not establish a matching account.

Rejected namesakes include the SGS Houston LinkedIn profile, Gaines County official Michael Lord Jr., Birchwood Credit Services' Austin executive, Toyota's engineer and British politician Michael Nicholson Lord. Shared name, state or industry adjacency is insufficient. The Sir Michael Lyons BBC figure is also unrelated.

No official personal or corporate website for his specific Lyons Petroleum Reserves entity was verified. The similarly named Florida Lyons Petroleum Inc. and historical Louisiana Lyons Petroleum businesses were not treated as his.

One approved active upstream tag is assigned for his substantial operating mandate, independently of the tentative personal-wealth inferences. Personal vessel companies do not support shipping, maritime-profession or yacht-charter industry tags.

The initial 2009 contract price was USD 400.384 million subject to adjustment; the 2010 completion filing reports USD 333 million cash paid at closing. Neither aggregate amount is used as personal wealth, and biographies omit deal values.
